title: Choose an estimator for a research design
skills: Matching estimand and estimator to the design

brief.text: Four research designs are described below. For the last one the data (SYNTHETIC) are loaded: a validated two-factor scale, eight continuous items, N = 500, about 8% of cells missing at random. Configure that analysis appropriately and run it.

tasks.prompt: Design A: managers define a "digital maturity" index from five components and want to explain and predict firm performance with it. Which approach fits best?

options.text: PLS-SEM with the index as a composite-formative construct
options.feedback: Correct. The construct is a designed composite and the goal includes prediction.

options.text: CB-SEM with the index as a common factor
options.feedback: A common factor assumes the components share one cause; an index does not.

options.text: PLSc, so that the index is corrected for measurement error
options.feedback: PLSc corrects only reflective constructs; a composite is left unchanged.

tasks.prompt: Design B: a reflective TAM model whose results are to be compared with published CB-SEM estimates, estimated with PLS. Which variant?

options.feedback: Correct. It targets the common-factor estimand that CB-SEM estimates.
Mode B is for composites and does not correct for measurement error.
The weighting scheme does not change the estimand.

tasks.prompt: Design C: a CFA of a scale with 4-point items that are strongly skewed. Which estimator does the literature recommend?

options.text: WLSMV on polychoric correlations, for example in R with lavaan (not available in SEM Lab's browser engine)
ML, because it is the default
options.feedback: With few, skewed categories, ML on raw scores can distort loadings and fit.
A CFA of a reflective scale targets common factors; classic PLS changes the estimand and ignores the ordinal nature as well.

tasks.prompt: Design D (loaded): configure CB-SEM so that all 500 cases are used under the missing-at-random assumption.
Run your Design D configuration and enter the standardised correlation of F1 and F2.
tasks.feedbackWrong: Not the expected value. A value near .35 means listwise deletion was used (258 cases); switch missing-data handling to FIML.

hints: First decide the estimand: is the construct a composite or a common factor?
Then the data: continuous or few ordinal categories? Complete or missing?
FIML needs a mean structure; SEM Lab adds it when you choose FIML, or tells you to.

solution.text: A: PLS-SEM with a composite-formative index. B: PLSc for common-factor estimates with PLS. C: an ordinal estimator such as WLSMV (available in R/lavaan, not in the browser engine).
D: CB-SEM, ML with FIML and a mean structure. It uses all 500 cases; the standardised factor correlation is ≈ .385 (listwise deletion would use 258 cases and give ≈ .353).
